title: Bar prism comparisons for the two cotangent functoriality arrows
statement:
Let $A\to B\to C$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings. Use the small identity-cover polynomial presentation sites, presheaves $F_1=F_{B/A}$, $F_2=F_{C/A}$, $F_3=F_{C/B}$ and pair-site short exact sequence $0\to M_1\xrightarrow a M_2\xrightarrow b M_3\to0$ of [lem-trf-cotangent-differential-presheaf-ses]. Put $X_i=K_{\mathcal E}^C(M_i)$ and let $c_i,\theta,\alpha_i$ be the canonical comparisons of [lem-trf-cotangent-bar-term-identifications], with bar maps as in [def-trf-derived-colimit-bar-system]. Define $h_1:\mathcal C_{B/A}\to\mathcal C_{C/A}$ by $(P\to B)\mapsto(P\to C)$, and $t_1:F_1\otimes_B C\to h_1^{-1}F_2$ by the identity identification of differential values. Define $h_2:\mathcal C_{C/A}\to\mathcal C_{C/B}$ by $(Q\to C)\mapsto(Q\otimes_A B\to C)$, and $t_2:F_2\to h_2^{-1}F_3$ by $\mathrm dq\otimes c\mapsto\mathrm d(q\otimes1)\otimes c$. In the opposite presentation categories, the maps $P\to Q$ and $Q\otimes_A B\to Q\otimes_P B$ define natural transformations $u_2\Rightarrow h_1u_1$ and $u_3\Rightarrow h_2u_2$, respectively. The following identities hold in $D(C)$:
$$c_2K_{\mathcal E}(a)=K(h_1,t_1)c_1,\qquad c_3K_{\mathcal E}(b)=K(h_2,t_2)c_2.$$
Here $K(h_i,t_i)$ is the derived map represented by reindexing bar chains and applying $t_i$ to the coefficient. Under $\theta$ and the scalar-change comparison, $K(h_1,t_1)$ is the scalar-adjoint standard cotangent map for $(A\to B)\to(A\to C)$, with tensor-generator rule $\mathrm dp\otimes r\otimes c\mapsto\mathrm dp\otimes rc$. Under $\theta$, $K(h_2,t_2)$ is the standard map for $(A\to C)\to(B\to C)$. Equivalently, if $f:L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C\to L_{C/A}$ and $g:L_{C/A}\to L_{C/B}$ are the standard maps of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence], then
$$\alpha_2K_{\mathcal E}(a)=f\alpha_1,\qquad\alpha_3K_{\mathcal E}(b)=g\alpha_2.$$
The identities hold for arbitrary ring maps, without injectivity or flatness assumptions.

source.place: Tag 08QL (section-functoriality), standard and sheaf descriptions of the maps, applied to the two maps in Tag 08QU (lemma-triangle-ses); sites-cohomology Tags 08PG/08PH (example-left-derived-colimits/example-morphism-categories), with the bar natural-transformation comparison.

proof.text: Work on the common small presentation skeletons stipulated in the differential-presheaf lemma; transport all formulas along their chosen presentation isomorphisms. If $P=A[x_s]$ then $h_1(P)$ is still polynomial over $A$; if $Q=A[z_t]$ then $h_2(Q)=B[z_t]$. Both augment to $C$. The coefficient maps $t_1,t_2$ are well-defined by the universal differential relations and tensor balancing. For a pair map $(\phi,\psi)$ before opposites, $\psi\iota=\iota'\phi$ for $\iota:P\to Q$. Hence these inclusions reverse to a natural transformation $\eta_1:u_2\Rightarrow h_1u_1$. Put $D=Q\otimes_P B$. The map $\mu:Q\otimes_A B\to D$, $q\otimes b\mapsto q\otimes b$, commutes with augmentations; for a pair map both composites send $q\otimes b$ to $\psi(q)\otimes b$. It reverses to $\eta_2:u_3\Rightarrow h_2u_2$. Naturality of $t_1,t_2$ follows since either route sends a differential generator to the differential of its image, with the same scalar. The universal construction of differentials states that these generators span.

source.place: Tag 08QL (section-functoriality), presentation-category description; Tag 08QU (lemma-triangle-ses), generator maps on the pair site.

proof.text: Apply the bar theorem's natural-transformation clause over $C$ with $v=u_2$, $w=h_1u_1$, $G=F_2$, $F=M_1$ and $t=u_1^{-1}t_1$. The coefficient map $F_2(\eta_1)t$ sends $(\mathrm dp\otimes r)\otimes c$ to $\mathrm d\iota(p)\otimes rc$, exactly $a_U$ in the differential-presheaf lemma. Thus its two homotopic maps are $K(u_2,1)K_{\mathcal E}(a)$ and $K(h_1,t_1)K(u_1,1)$. Composition of bar maps is the generatorwise composition asserted by that theorem. The term-identification lemma identifies the two reindexing maps with $c_2$ and $c_1$ (for $c_1$, use $F_1\otimes_B C$). Equality of the localized homotopic maps gives $c_2K_{\mathcal E}(a)=K(h_1,t_1)c_1$.

source.place: Tags 08PG (example-left-derived-colimits), 08PH (example-morphism-categories); natural-transformation prism expansion in the cited bar theorem.

proof.text: For the second prism use $v=u_3$, $w=h_2u_2$, $G=F_3$, $F=M_2$ and $t=u_2^{-1}t_2$. The restriction $F_3(\eta_2)$ is induced by $\mu:Q\otimes_A B\to D$ and sends $\mathrm d(q\otimes1)\otimes c$ to $\mathrm d(q\otimes1)\otimes c$ in $\Omega_{D/B}\otimes_D C$. Under the differential-presheaf lemma's third identification this is $\mathrm d_{Q/P}q\otimes c$, exactly $b_U(\mathrm d_{Q/A}q\otimes c)$. Consequently $F_3(\eta_2)t=b$ on the generating differentials and hence everywhere. The bar theorem gives equality of $K(u_3,1)K_{\mathcal E}(b)$ and $K(h_2,t_2)K(u_2,1)$ in $D(C)$. Substitution of the stated $c_3,c_2$ yields $c_3K_{\mathcal E}(b)=K(h_2,t_2)c_2$.

source.place: Tags 08PG (example-left-derived-colimits), 08PH (example-morphism-categories); natural-transformation prism expansion in the cited bar theorem.

proof.text: Apply the sheaf-model functoriality identity to the square $(A\to C)\to(B\to C)$ with vertical maps $A\to B$ and $1_C$. Its indexing functor and coefficient map are exactly $h_2,t_2$, so $\theta_{C/B}K(h_2,t_2)=g\theta_{C/A}$. For the square $(A\to B)\to(A\to C)$ with base map $1_A$, its indexing functor sends $P$ to $P\otimes_A A$, canonically isomorphic to $h_1(P)=P$ by $p\otimes a\mapsto ap$. These isomorphisms commute with every presentation map and send $\mathrm d(p\otimes1)$ to $\mathrm dp$. The bar theorem's natural-isomorphism clause therefore identifies this square's semilinear bar map with $\gamma=K(h_1,t_0)$, where $t_0(\mathrm dp\otimes r)=\mathrm dp\otimes\beta(r)$ and $\beta:B\to C$. Writing $\gamma^{\rm std}:L_{B/A}\to\operatorname{Res}_{\beta}L_{C/A}$ for the standard map, the sheaf-model identity says $\theta_{C/A}\gamma=\gamma^{\rm std}\theta_{B/A}$ in $D(B)$, with target scalars restricted. The coherence lemma fixes these standard maps for both squares.

proof.text:
Put $Y=K_{\mathcal C_{B/A}}^B(F_1)$ and $Z=K_{\mathcal C_{B/A}}^C(F_1\otimes_B C)$, and write $\Phi:Z\simeq Y\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C$ for the scalar-change comparison. The term-identification lemma gives flatness of every $F_1(P)$; the objectwise-flat bar lemma then gives K-flatness with flat terms of both $F_1[0]$ and $Y$. Thus the bar scalar-unit-transpose lemma applies: if $j:Y\to\operatorname{Res}_{\beta}Z$ sends $(\sigma,x)$ to $(\sigma,x\otimes1)$, its adjunct is $\Phi^{-1}$. This is the same $\Phi$ as the change-of-rings lemma, with its displayed generator formula. Set $T=K(h_1,t_1)$. On generators $Tj=\gamma$ from step 4. Naturality of the normalized adjunction in its target implies that the adjunct of $\gamma$ is $T\Phi^{-1}$. Transposing the equality of step 4, and using naturality in its source as well, gives
$$\theta_{C/A}T\Phi^{-1}=f(\theta_{B/A}\otimes^{\mathbf L}1),$$
where $f$ is the scalar adjunct of $\gamma^{\rm std}$. Equivalently $\theta_{C/A}T=f(\theta_{B/A}\otimes^{\mathbf L}1)\Phi$. In these tensor representatives the coefficient rule is $(\mathrm dp\otimes r)\otimes c\mapsto\mathrm dp\otimes\beta(r)c$, by the definition of $t_1$. This proves the asserted scalar-adjoint identification without assuming $\beta$ flat.

source.place: Tags 08Q8 (lemma-change-of-rings), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), with the normalized bar scalar-unit transpose of the cited nodes; cotangent Tag 08QL, scalar adjunct of the first arrow.

proof.text: Finally substitute the term-identification lemma's formulas $\alpha_1=(\theta_{B/A}\otimes^{\mathbf L}1)\Phi c_1$, $\alpha_2=\theta_{C/A}c_2$ and $\alpha_3=\theta_{C/B}c_3$ into steps 2--5. Associativity gives $\alpha_2K_{\mathcal E}(a)=f\alpha_1$ and $\alpha_3K_{\mathcal E}(b)=g\alpha_2$. The prism applications used only smallness and naturality; the scalar comparison used flat values of $F_1$, already supplied independently of $B\to C$. Thus every identity holds for arbitrary ring maps.
